title: Let the right person see the right data
outcome: Enforce ownership on the service, including cross-shop failures.
story: Amina’s customers should see their own orders. Her staff can help customers in her shop. A staff member from another shop still cannot see Amina’s orders.

frames.action: Sign in as the order’s customer
frames.explanation: A known identity is the beginning of a permission check.
A staff role does not grant permission across every shop.

sections.title: Identify the person
paragraphs: Authentication establishes who is making a request. A service may verify a password and issue a session cookie. Later requests use that session to obtain the identity on the server.

Never accept a client’s user id, shop, or role as proof of identity. In the browser exercise the user dictionary is a trusted fixture supplied by the test. In the project, it must come from a verified server session.

sections.title: Decide what that person may do
paragraphs: Authorization checks permission for a specific operation and record. First deny missing identity. Next require the same shop. Finally allow shop staff or the customer who owns the order.

Keep the order important in the check: permission for order 1 does not imply permission for order 2. Check every read and write endpoint. Hiding a button in the interface does not prevent a direct request.

sections.title: Keep credentials and input controlled
paragraphs: Use a proven password hashing method with a salt and appropriate work factor. Store session tokens carefully, expire sessions, and invalidate them on logout. Production cookies need HTTPS, Secure, HttpOnly, and a considered SameSite policy.

A cookie-based write also needs protection against cross-site requests. The service workspace uses a CSRF token for state-changing requests. Validate input and bind database parameters even after authentication: a signed-in user can still send bad data.

sections.title: Test denied cases explicitly
paragraphs: Test a missing session, another customer in the same shop, a customer in another shop, and staff in another shop. A useful permission test proves the denied request cannot read or change the target record.

Choose a consistent response policy, including whether unauthorized callers can learn that a record exists. Keep detailed reasons out of public errors. Record a safe denial event with a request id rather than a password or session token.

words.meaning: Deciding whether that person may perform a particular action.
A server-verified sign-in record used across requests.

explanation: A missing or mismatched shop is rejected first.
Staff permission is scoped to the shop.
A customer must own this particular order.

exercise.title: An order permission rule
exercise.brief: Write can_read(user, order). Deny missing identity, require a non-empty matching shop, and then allow staff or the owning customer.

steps.title: Require an identity
steps.task: Return False for None and True for the supplied same-shop staff example.
steps.hint: None means that authentication did not provide an identity.
steps.solution:
def can_read(user, order):
    return user is not None

steps.title: Keep shops separate
steps.task: Require user.shop and order.shop to match.
steps.hint: Compare shops before deciding whether a role grants permission.
steps.solution:
def can_read(user, order):
    return user is not None and user.get("shop") == order.get("shop")

steps.title: Check role or ownership
steps.task: Require a non-empty shop. In that shop allow staff, or a user whose id matches customer_id.
steps.hint: Use the final two conditions only after the shop check passes.

cases.label: Amina’s staff
cases.why: Staff can support their own shop.

cases.label: Another shop’s staff
cases.why: The shop boundary comes before the role.

cases.label: The owning customer
cases.why: Customers can read their own order.

cases.label: Another customer in the same shop
cases.why: Same shop alone is insufficient for a customer.

cases.label: Missing shop fields
cases.why: Two missing values must not count as a valid shop match.

project.title: A service with scoped access
project.brief: Run the service workspace with two shops and two customer accounts. Connect permission checks to every protected endpoint.
deliverables: An access matrix for roles and operations.

milestones.title: Establish identity
actions: Inspect the workspace password and session implementation.
Sign in using a prepared local account.
Verify that logout invalidates the session.

milestones.title: Enforce access
actions: Obtain identity from the verified session.
Apply a shop and record check on each endpoint.
Prevent request fields from changing ownership.

milestones.title: Attempt denied requests
actions: Use another customer session to request the record.
Verify denied writes leave the database unchanged.

acceptance: Identity comes from a verified session.
Customers see only their permitted records.
Staff access stays within their shop.
Cookie-based writes require the CSRF token.
Logs omit passwords and session tokens.
project.extension: Add an expiry test with a controlled clock and document how production HTTPS and cookie settings differ from localhost.
reflection: Why is hiding a button insufficient?
Where does trusted identity come from?
Which test proves a denied write did nothing?
